thought.text: CSRF passed, but login says credentials failed / email verification. The password may differ from "test" for the auto_wizard-seeded user. Let me check the auto_wizard definition:

reasoning_content:
Interesting! The CSRF check passed (we got past CSRF), but login failed: "Login failed. Have you double-checked your credentials and completed the email verification step?"

This suggests that either the admin@example.com password is not "test", or the user has not completed email verification. In Zammad, users may need to confirm their email address before being able to log in. The auto_wizard created the users, but maybe email confirmation is required.

Wait — the guide says that the default development credentials are admin@example.com / test. Let me investigate. Maybe the password isn't "test" — it might be something that the auto_wizard sets. Let me check the auto_wizard definition.

Actually, the message mentions "completed the email verification step". In Zammad, if the "Verify emails" setting is enabled, users need to confirm via email. But in development, emails are usually not verified.

Let me reconsider. It's possible that the password for the admin user created by auto_wizard is different. Let me look for the auto_wizard JSON that defines the users.

Let me search for auto_wizard in the repository.

action.command: find /workspace -iname "*auto_wizard*" 2>/dev/null | grep -v node_modules; echo "=== search for admin@example.com in json ==="; grep -rln "admin@example.com" /workspace --include="*.json" 2>/dev/null | grep -v node_modules | head
